stops.note: literally 'what has been spoken' (by the gods), from fari 'to speak'; Virgil's Aeneid opens with Aeneas 'fato profugus', exiled by fate
'fate' gave its name to a mournful song style born in Lisbon's Alfama and Mouraria districts; Maria Severa (1820-1846) is its first legendary singer
Amália Rodrigues's international tours from the 1950s carried it abroad, and UNESCO listed fado as Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2011

current_meaning: a melancholy Portuguese folk song, typically about longing and fate
